what_it_does: Designing analog circuits — circuits that deal with continuously varying voltages rather than just on/off signals — currently requires running detailed physics-based simulations (called SPICE simulations, after the industry-standard tool) thousands of times to explore how different component choices affect performance. These simulations are slow and expensive, making automated design-space search impractical. Opera addresses this by training a surrogate model — a lightweight neural network that learns to mimic the simulator's outputs far faster than the real simulator — and plugging it in wherever the optimizer would normally call SPICE. The surrogate-equipped optimizer is wrapped in an interface modeled on OpenAI Gym (a standard environment format used in reinforcement learning research), so existing optimization algorithms can plug in easily. Crucially, the whole platform is built on an open-source 45-nanometer semiconductor process definition, so researchers can reproduce results without access to proprietary chip-foundry data. This is a late-breaking results paper (a brief summary), so full benchmarks are not yet available.
